title: All auth routes and validators
idea: `auth.routes.js` lists every endpoint with its guards in order: `verifyJWT` if secured, then the rules, then `validate`, then the controller.

analogy.text: A clinic front desk. The receptionist checks your ID, then your forms, and only then sends you to the doctor.
analogy.breaks: A clinic checks once per visit; every request here repeats every check.

points: One router holds every endpoint; `app.js` mounts it at `/api/v1/auth`.
Each route lists its guards in run order: `verifyJWT`, rules, `validate`, controller.
Public routes skip `verifyJWT`. Email links and the refresh cookie carry their own tokens.
Five validators share small helper rules; login checks presence, never strength.

parts.label: Path
parts.note: The path inside `/api/v1/auth`. `app.use` in `app.js` adds the prefix.

parts.label: Method
parts.note: Only `POST` matches. The same path with `GET` gets `404`.

parts.label: 1st: who
parts.note: Runs first. Without a valid access token the answer is `401`, and nothing below runs.

parts.label: 2nd: rules
parts.note: Rules for `oldPassword` and `newPassword`. They record errors and reject nothing.

parts.label: 3rd: verdict
parts.note: Throws `ApiError(422)` when any rule recorded an error.

parts.label: 4th: controller
parts.note: Runs only if every guard passed.

parts.label: Close
parts.note: Public routes drop the first guard: `post(rules(), validate, controller)`.

code.title: validators and routes
code.caption: The two project files of this lesson, with stub controllers. Press Run: every route with an empty body, then the order of guards.

walk.text: Condensed from earlier lessons: `ApiError`, `validate`, a `verifyJWT` stand-in and ten stub controllers.
Three helper rules: `email()`, `text()` for presence and type, and `strong()` for length.
Five validators from them, plus a custom rule on register. Login uses `text`, so older passwords still work.
Register and login get rules. `verify-email` and `refresh-token` have none: they read a URL token or a cookie.
Forgot and reset get rules too: the email, or the new password, comes in the body.
Secured routes put `verifyJWT` first. `/refresh-token` is not one: its access token has expired.
Ten routes with no cookie, then `change-password` with one: guards run in order.

code.title: verifyEmail, getCurrentUser
code.caption: The last two controllers, which no earlier lesson wrote. Press Run: a wrong link, the right one, a replay.

walk.text: Condensed: utils, a `sha256` helper and a trimmed `User`.
Hash the URL token and look for an unexpired match, as the reset does. No match is `400`.
Mark the email verified and clear the token fields, so the link works once.
Both routes join the router; a stand-in sets `req.user`.
Seed a pending user, then try a wrong link, the right link and a replay.

pitfalls: Do not guard `/refresh-token` with `verifyJWT`: it is called when the access token has expired.
Put `verifyJWT` before the rules: strangers should see `401`, not field-level `422` errors.
Test each guard separately: one request for `401`, one for `422`, one for success.

quiz.why: `verifyJWT` runs before the rules. Without a cookie the request stops at `401`; with one, the missing `newPassword` gives `422`.

takeaway: Order the guards: who you are, then what you sent, then the work.

starters: Can one validator serve several routes?
How do I split a growing router into several files?
